ops.note:
An unknown verdict now demotes rather than keeping the lane, and always sets a note. Verified live (ccx v0.39.0) with a hanging `gt` shim: `lane` = `git`, `lane_reason` = `"graphite declined: gt auth did not answer within 20s"`. The demotion is never silent — a demoted lane names its reason on the ship report line, as it already did for an outright refusal.

This is the behavioral inversion the fix turns on: v0.35.0 mapped unknown to `reachable = true` and kept the gt lane, which made the gate a no-op. Three tests were deliberately inverted to argue the new case rather than merely flipping assertions — `TestShipGateProbeTimeoutDemotes` (renamed from `…KeepsGT`), and `TestShipGateProbe`'s "server unreachable" and "authenticated outside a repo" subtests, both of which previously asserted the lane was kept.

Cost measured rather than assumed: one probe per command, ~25s worst case when gt never answers (20s cap + 5s `WaitDelay` reaping the forked grandchild), and the unknown verdict caches for 60s so an outage costs that once a minute rather than once per command.
